vote.question: FUTARCHY CONDITIONAL RESOLUTION [US-MI U.S. Senate]: Abdul El-sayed (D) has accumulated $53,830,872 in career FEC-reported receipts (anchored this cycle by Smp ($182,790,000) and $185,904,609 from top-5 patrons)—out-raising general opponent Michael J Rogers ($23,016,439) by 2.34x—exhibiting the "Defense, Aerospace & Surveillance Contractor Bloc" profile. Will independent constituent & oracle review confirm that this private-interest capital concentration compromises public representation in US-MI, thereby executing the MI Corrective Restitution Pool toward veterans' trauma/housing rehabilitation and digital privacy civil-liberties defense?
vote.futarchy_thesis: Private campaign financing treats US-MI representation as an investable asset class. When Abdul El-sayed's campaign apparatus absorbs $53,830,872 (anchored this cycle by Smp ($182,790,000) and $185,904,609 from top-5 patrons), policy incentives skew toward perpetual procurement escalation and domestic surveillance expansion over local infrastructure. This futarchy market converts spectator outrage into direct fiscal counter-leverage.
options: Yes — Confirm Capture & Execute State Restitution Bounty
No — Veto Capture Claim & Roll Escrow Pool to Bipartisan Commons
Abstain — Log On-Chain Constituent Dissent Only

If the No option wins, funds redirect to a bipartisan district-wide common good that strengthens the entire community — denying special interests the ability to commandeer the bounty and promoting positive-sum governance over zero-sum subjugation.
